headline: India blocks entry of PM's advisor at Delhi airport
summary: Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman was held for 2.5 hours by immigration authorities before deciding to return to Dhaka via Colombo.
details: Prime Minister's Advisor on Policy and Strategy, Zahed Ur Rahman, was blocked from entering Delhi on Sunday evening despite prior diplomatic notification.
Rahman was traveling to lead the Bangladesh delegation at the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) senior officials' meeting starting Monday.
Upon arrival at Indira Gandhi International Airport, immigration authorities held him for two and a half hours for 'mysterious reasons' without clarifying if entry would be granted.
Although permission was later granted following orders from higher authorities, Rahman decided not to enter the city and instead departed for Colombo on his way back to Dhaka.
The Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi had officially informed the Indian Ministry of External Affairs about his participation as the delegation leader last Friday.
caption:
Held for 2.5 hours at the airport: Why was the PM's advisor blocked from entering India?

Prime Minister's Advisor on Policy and Strategy, Zahed Ur Rahman, was blocked from entering Delhi on Sunday evening despite prior diplomatic notification.

Rahman was traveling to lead the Bangladesh delegation at the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) senior officials' meeting starting Monday.

Upon arrival at Indira Gandhi International Airport, immigration authorities held him for two and a half hours for 'mysterious reasons' without clarifying if entry would be granted.

Although permission was later granted following orders from higher authorities, Rahman decided not to enter the city and instead departed for Colombo on his way back to Dhaka.

The Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi had officially informed the Indian Ministry of External Affairs about his participation as the delegation leader last Friday.

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: 64-run win: [[India rout Pakistan]] at women's T20 World Cup
headline: 64-run win: India rout Pakistan at women's T20 World Cup
summary: Smriti Mandhana's 68 and Deepti Sharma's 5-wicket haul lead India to a dominant victory in their opening match.
details: India secured a dominant 64-run victory over arch-rivals Pakistan in their opening group game of the women's T20 World Cup at Edgbaston.
Opener Smriti Mandhana led the charge with 68 runs from 44 balls, including nine fours and two sixes, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur added 36.
Wicket-keeper Richa Ghosh further pressured the Pakistani bowlers with a quick-fire 34, helping India set a formidable target.
Pakistan's run chase collapsed against India's spinners, with all-rounder Deepti Sharma delivering a masterclass performance, finishing with figures of 5-10.
Leg-spinner Sree Charani also contributed significantly, taking three wickets as Pakistan slumped from 75-3 to 79-6.
Pakistan captain Fatima Sana expressed disappointment in the batting performance and highlighted missed catches as a critical factor in the loss.
The match set a new attendance record for a women's T20 World Cup group stage game, with 18,814 fans in attendance.
caption:
India dominates Pakistan in a record-breaking crowd setting! Deepti Sharma's 5-wicket haul seals the rout.

India secured a dominant 64-run victory over arch-rivals Pakistan in their opening group game of the women's T20 World Cup at Edgbaston.

Opener Smriti Mandhana led the charge with 68 runs from 44 balls, including nine fours and two sixes, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur added 36.

Wicket-keeper Richa Ghosh further pressured the Pakistani bowlers with a quick-fire 34, helping India set a formidable target.

Pakistan's run chase collapsed against India's spinners, with all-rounder Deepti Sharma delivering a masterclass performance, finishing with figures of 5-10.

Leg-spinner Sree Charani also contributed significantly, taking three wickets as Pakistan slumped from 75-3 to 79-6.

Pakistan captain Fatima Sana expressed disappointment in the batting performance and highlighted missed catches as a critical factor in the loss.

The match set a new attendance record for a women's T20 World Cup group stage game, with 18,814 fans in attendance.
